4.7 Microbusiness and Class A microbusiness (adult-use only)

These are the only vertically integrated single-licence types in Michigan. Both are single-location licences and may not operate at multiple locations.

Marihuana Microbusiness (standard): - Cultivate not more than 150 marihuana plants; process and package marihuana; sell/transfer marihuana to individuals 21+ or to a marihuana safety compliance facility, but not to other marihuana establishments. MRTMA §3 definition: "a person licensed to cultivate not more than 150 marihuana plants; process and package marihuana; and sell or otherwise transfer marihuana to individuals who are 21 years of age or older or to a marihuana safety compliance facility, but not to other marihuana establishments." Source: https://komornlaw.com/michigan-regulation-and-taxation-of-marihuana-act-section-3-2/ — Accessed 2026-10-28. - May not purchase from other licensees (other than the narrow caregiver-transfer-on-licensure exception in R. 420.105 and seeds/tissue cultures/clones/plants from another grower for a Class A microbusiness — see below; for standard microbusiness the purchase ban is the defining limit). A standard microbusiness therefore cannot wholesale its product to retailers. - Fee: $8,300 initial + $8,300 renewal, plus $3,000 prequalification. Source: R. 420.7 Table 1 — Accessed 2026-10-28. - Holding another licence: "A marijuana microbusiness licensee holding other cannabis licenses in Michigan violates Section 9 of the MRTMA, MCL 333.27959" (secondary summary, https://michigancannabis.org/licensing/microbusiness — Accessed 2026-10-28) — [VERIFY] against MCL 333.27959 text in Part 1; the rule compilation (R. 420.105) subjects a microbusiness to grower, retailer and processor provisions except R. 420.102(8), which is consistent with a stand-alone, non-stacked model.

Class A Marihuana Microbusiness: - Cultivate not more than 300 plants (only mature plants counted); package marihuana; purchase marihuana concentrate and marihuana-infused products from a licensed marihuana processor; sell/transfer marihuana and marihuana products to individuals 21+ only; transfer to a safety compliance facility for testing. R. 420.105a(1) as reproduced at https://420tax.github.io/michigan-cannabis-compliance/rules/latest/ — Accessed 2026-10-28. - May transfer marihuana between its own grower area and retailer area without a secure transporter if all areas enter each transfer into the statewide monitoring system (R. 420.105a(2), same source). - Shall not operate at multiple locations (R. 420.105a(3), same source). - May purchase/accept seeds, tissue cultures, clones or plants from another grower (R. 420.105a(5), same source). - Fee: $18,600 initial + $18,600 renewal, plus $3,000 prequalification. Source: R. 420.7 Table 1 — Accessed 2026-10-28. (An older 2020 RIS form listed Class A microbusiness at $8,600 — superseded; see §4.1.) - Difference in one line: Class A = 300 plants + may buy concentrates/infused products from processors; standard = 150 plants + may not buy from other establishments. Both sell only to consumers 21+ (and to testing labs), not wholesale.

Applications open or capped? Open statewide, subject to municipal authorisation. Counts are tiny (see Part 5: 6 standard + 10 Class A adult-use licences in Sept 2025), which reflects economics and the no-wholesale limit, not a statutory cap.

It is not a retailer: it does not by itself authorise retail sale unless separately licensed as a retailer/microbusiness. $1,000 initial + $1,000 renewal, plus $3,000 prequalification Lowest adult-use fee in Table 1. (b) For temporary marihuana events that include the sale of marihuana products: (i) A $500.00 fee for each licensee authorized to sell marihuana product at the event … (ii) A $500.00 fee for each day of the temporary marihuana event … (3) A marihuana event organizer applicant is not required to pay an application fee." N/A in R. 420.7 Table 1; no $3,000 application fee is shown for this type in Table 1 Only 1 active licence in Sept 2025 (Part 5). Eligibility, application form and any institutional requirements are [VERIFY] — no CRA educational-research instruction sheet was directly opened in this session. Do not assume it is open to commercial applicants; by name and by count it is an institutional research licence.

4.9 Stacking, co-location and ownership rules (summary for Part 4; full transfer/ownership rules are Part 11)

  • Grower stacking: Unlimited in number in principle; each licence carries its own plant allowance (§4.2). Excess grower is itself a stacking product (5 adult-use Class C + ≥2 medical Class C, §4.3).
  • Equivalent licences across programmes: A person may hold the medical and adult-use equivalents at the same premises (R. 420.1 "equivalent licenses," §4.5). They remain separate licences, separately fee'd, separately counted, and product must not be moved between the medical and adult-use inventories except as the rules and Metrc allow — a compliance point repeatedly enforced (see Part 5 disciplinary examples).
  • Microbusinesses do not stack with other licences: A microbusiness (either class) is a single-location, stand-alone licence; holding another marihuana licence alongside it is prohibited under MRTMA §9 (MCL 333.27959) per the secondary summary cited in §4.7 [VERIFY against statute text].
  • Safety compliance independence: A testing lab and its investors may not hold interests in the businesses it tests (§4.6, [VERIFY]).
  • No licence as property/collateral: Under the MMFLA, a licence is not a property right and cannot be pledged as collateral; the same principle is stated in the rules for MRTMA licences (draft-rules commentary, [VERIFY] against current R. 420.6). Transfers and ownership changes are therefore CRA-approved transactions, not private assignments — full detail is Part 11.

4.10 Medical (MMFLA) fees and assessments — what is confirmed, what is not

Confirmed structure: - MMFLA application fee: MCL 333.27401(5) (MMFLA §401) sets an application fee (the CRA FY2024 report's fee table is the last directly opened CRA fee table in this session). The regulatory assessment is separate and annual: MCL 333.27603(3) provides "The regulatory assessment shall be collected annually from licensed growers, processors, provisioning centers, and secure transporters. The regulatory assessment for a class A grower license shall not exceed $10,000.00." and §603(4)–(5) requires the department to set the total assessment annually at an amount estimated to cover actual costs, with each licensee paying its reasonably apportioned share on or before beginning operations and annually thereafter. Source: R. 420.7 via Cornell — Accessed 2026-10-28. - Safety compliance facilities pay no medical regulatory assessment (FY2024 table, §4.6). - An MMFLA applicant must pay the regulatory assessment within 10 days after the CRA determines the applicant meets all requirements for a state operating licence (R. 420.7(6) analogue / older rule text, §4.1).

4.11 Social equity programme (CRA, MRTMA §9 / MCL 333.27958)

Legal basis. MRTMA §9 (MCL 333.27958(1)(j)) directs the CRA to develop a plan "to promote and encourage participation in the marijuana industry by people from communities that have been disproportionately impacted by marijuana prohibition and enforcement and to positively impact those communities." The CRA programme implements that direction through fee reductions, education/outreach and application assistance (all three are separately counted in CRA monthly reports — see Part 5, §5.2).

Who qualifies — majority ownership + one criterion. The applicant business must be majority-owned (>50%) by persons meeting at least one criterion. Fee reductions (on adult-use application and licensure/renewal fees — i.e. the $3,000 prequalification fee and the R. 420.7 Table 1 fees):

Criterion Fee reduction
Resided in a CRA-designated disproportionately impacted community for at least 5 cumulative years within the past 10 years 25%
Marijuana-related misdemeanor conviction (even if later expunged) 25%
Marijuana-related felony conviction (even if later expunged), excluding distribution to a minor 40%
Registered primary caregiver under the MMMA for at least 2 years between 2008 and 2017 10%

Reductions stack to a maximum of 75%. Worked example: a $15,000 retailer fee at 75% reduction = $3,750; a $24,000 Class C fee at 75% = $6,000; the $3,000 prequalification fee at 75% = $750. (Arithmetic by this report; the percentages are the sourced facts.)

How long the reduction lasts — the place rule. If the social-equity business operates inside a disproportionately impacted community, the reduction applies for as long as it holds the licence. If it operates outside such a community, the reduction applies for only the first two years after licensure, after which full fees apply. Applicants should apply to the Social Equity Programme before submitting Step 1 prequalification (CRA guidance as summarised in secondary sources — [VERIFY] against the CRA programme page).

Sources for criteria, percentages, stacking cap and duration: CRA programme as summarised consistently across https://www.covasoftware.com/us-dispensary-laws/Michigan, https://legalclarity.org/michigan-cannabis-licensing-types-process-and-compliance/, and https://divinetoke.org/blog/detroit-social-equity-check-in-fall-2026/ — all Accessed 2026-10-28. The CRA's own social-equity programme page was not directly opened in this session, so these percentages are secondary-sourced and marked [VERIFY] against michigan.gov/cra's social-equity page before republication as CRA-confirmed. The consistency across three independent secondary summaries makes the percentages high-confidence but not "directly opened" under this dossier's sourcing rule.

Eligible communities — method and count. The CRA identifies 184 communities as disproportionately impacted. Method (as described in the Senate Fiscal Agency's "OneFAB" social-equity brief, which reproduces the CRA criteria): communities where marijuana convictions (excluding distribution to a minor) are above the state median and at least 20% of the population lives below the federal poverty level (threshold lowered from 30% to 20% effective 1 June 2020 in the MRA expansion). Source: https://sfa.senate.michigan.gov/Publications/OneFAB/2025/OneFAB06-23-2025jm.pdf — Accessed 2026-10-28; corroborating 184-community list at https://komornlaw.com/category/blog/news/page/15/ — Accessed 2026-10-28.

What social equity is not. It is not a separate licence type, not a cap exemption, not a municipal licence, and not a retail price discount: it reduces CRA application/licensure fees only. Detroit's separate "Detroit Legacy" programme (city-level, with its own residency/conviction criteria and city-fee reductions) is a municipal programme, not the CRA programme, and is covered in Part 3/Part 5 local records, not here.

Social-equity grants. Secondary reporting (CannBus Q3 2026, citing CRA/official sources) states a $1 million-per-year grant pool shared equally among qualifying equity licensees: 62 shared it in 2024 and 103 in 2025. Source: https://www.cannbus.org/cannmir/mi_cannmir.html — Accessed 2026-10-28 [VERIFY against CRA grant announcements; the monthly-report "Social Equity" sections count applications/education/assistance, not grant dollars].

4.12 Requirements common to applicants (summary; detail is Parts 1 and 11)

  • Age/eligibility: Applicants and supplemental applicants undergo fingerprint-based background checks (CRA Step 1 instructions; fingerprints only after CRA notification — pre-notification fingerprint records are not accepted). Certain felony convictions and other ineligibility grounds in R. 420.6/R. 420.12 can support denial — [VERIFY] current ineligibility list against R. 420.6 before republication.
  • Financial responsibility (insurance/bond): Before issuance/renewal, an applicant/licensee must file proof of financial responsibility for bodily-injury liability from adulterated marihuana/products of not less than $100,000 (insurance policy from a licensed insurer/captive in Michigan, insured = licensee). MMFLA licensees must additionally carry commercial general liability insurance for premises liability of not less than $100,000, proof provided no later than 60 days after issuance/renewal. Source: rules compilation (R. 420.10) at https://www.cannabis-law-blog.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2026/05/Redline-March-2025-DraftRules-and-DraftRuleVersion_6_05.06.26.pdf — Accessed 2026-10-28 [VERIFY against current R. 420.10].
  • MMFLA capitalisation (medical only): R. 420.11 requires CPA-attested proof of total capitalisation, ≥25% in liquid assets: Grower Class A $150,000; Class B $300,000; Class C $500,000; Processor $300,000; Provisioning Center $300,000; Secure Transporter $200,000; Safety Compliance Facility $200,000. Source: https://regulations.justia.com/states/michigan/licensing-and-regulatory-affairs/marijuana-regulatoty-agency/marihuana-licenses/section-r-420-11/ — Accessed 2026-10-28. There is no equivalent MRTMA capitalisation schedule in R. 420.11 (it is headed "medical marihuana facilities licensing act"); adult-use applicants instead demonstrate financial responsibility and business-plan viability through Step 1/Step 2. Do not apply the medical capitalisation figures to adult-use applicants.
  • Municipal authorisation, zoning, security, Metrc, fire/Bureau of Fire Services plan review (growers and specified categories), and inspection readiness within 60 days of Step 2 — see §§4.0, 4.2 and Part 3/Part 11.

4.13 Hemp licences (brief here; full detail is Part 7)

Two distinct hemp authorisations exist in Michigan; neither is a marihuana licence, and neither appears in R. 420.7.

A. MDARD Industrial Hemp Grower Registration (grower registration, not a "licence" in the CRA sense). - Issuer: Michigan Department of Agriculture and Rural Development (MDARD), Pesticide and Plant Pest Management Division, under the Industrial Hemp Growers Act, 2020 PA 220, operating under Michigan's USDA-approved state hemp plan (USDA plan list, updated 17 Feb 2026, lists "Michigan — MI Approved Plan"). Source: https://www.ams.usda.gov/rules-regulations/hemp/state-and-tribal-plan-review — Accessed 2026-10-28; plan text: https://www.ams.usda.gov/sites/default/files/media/MichiganStateHempPlan.pdf — Accessed 2026-10-28. - What it allows: Grow hemp (only); sell harvested hemp to a licensed hemp processor or a licensed marijuana processor. It does not authorise processing, handling, brokering or marketing finished hemp products — that needs the processor-handler licence below. - Fees (current, secondary-sourced from MDARD fee sheet as summarised 2026): $1,250 nonrefundable grower registration application fee (initial and renewal); $250 late fee on renewals after 31 January; $50 per growing-location modification form; $150 per site visit for preharvest/remediation sampling; $150 per sample tested at MDARD's Geagley Lab (new from 1 January 2026). Registration cycle: 1 February – 31 January (2026 cycle: 1 Feb 2026 – 31 Jan 2027). Source: https://sativauniversity.com/cannabis-laws/michigan/ and https://legalclarity.org/how-to-legally-grow-hemp-in-michigan/ — both Accessed 2026-10-28 [VERIFY against MDARD's current "Industrial Hemp Program Fees" sheet; the MDARD fee page itself was not directly opened]. Superseded figure: the 2019–2020 pilot fee was $100 (MSU Extension hemp page, https://msu-prod.dotcmscloud.com/hemp/index — Accessed 2026-10-28, describing the 2020 pilot); $100 is NOT the current fee. - Requirements (summary): Business/key-participant information; GPS coordinates (to six decimal places) and legal description for each field/greenhouse/building; satellite-view maps; FBI Identity History Summary for each key participant dated within 60 days of application; preharvest THC sampling 20–30 days before harvest; no disqualifying felony drug conviction in the past 10 years for key participants (per MDARD programme summaries — [VERIFY] against PA 220 text). MDARD must approve/deny a completed application within 120 days (USDA state-plan summary — [VERIFY]). - Applications open or capped? Open; "no limit on the number of licenses issued or the number of acres grown" (MSU Extension summary of the pilot programme, same URL — the no-limit principle is carried into the state plan; [VERIFY] against PA 220).

B. CRA Hemp Processor-Handler Licence. - Issuer: Cannabis Regulatory Agency, under the Industrial Hemp Research and Development Act, 2014 PA 547, following Executive Reorganization Order 2022-1 (which moved hemp processing oversight to the CRA). Note the issuer history: older MDARD pages still show a MDARD mailing address for processor-handler forms; current issuer is the CRA. - What it requires / allows: Required for processing raw hemp into marketable form; possessing, storing or transporting industrial hemp; brokering hemp; promoting/selling (marketing) hemp, a hemp commodity or product — including retail sale. Both in-state and out-of-state hemp retailers marketing in Michigan need it. Individual hemp products are not separately registered. Sampling/testing hemp alone does not require it. Source: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDARD/bulletins/2f69c1a and https://michigancannabis.org/cannabis-business — both Accessed 2026-10-28. - Fee: $1,350 nonrefundable, initial and renewal; $250 late fee for renewals submitted after 30 November. Licence year: 1 December – 30 November. Sources: https://sativauniversity.com/cannabis-laws/michigan/, https://michigancannabis.org/hemp, https://legalclarity.org/how-to-legally-grow-hemp-in-michigan/ — all Accessed 2026-10-28 [VERIFY against the CRA hemp processor-handler fee page; the CRA FAQ cited by secondary sources lists the same $1,350 / Dec 1–Nov 30 figures]. - Applications open or capped? Open; no cap stated. - Cross-reference: Full hemp licence detail, including the post-11 December 2026 federal total-THC definition's effect on what counts as hemp vs. marihuana, is Part 7. A hemp processor-handler licence does not authorise handling marihuana, and a marihuana processor licence does not by itself authorise all hemp processor-handler activities (see §4.4).

4.14 Estimated startup costs — NON-OFFICIAL estimates only

No Michigan agency publishes an official startup-cost schedule. The figures below are non-official, secondary estimates and must be labelled as such in the parent dossier. They exclude the value of acquiring an existing licence/business, which in saturated markets can exceed build-out cost.

Segment (non-official) Estimate Source / date
Adult-use retailer (dispensary) — total, low end ~$300,000 IndicaOnline, "How to Open a Dispensary in Michigan" (updated 2026; page last updated ~115 days before 2026-10-28): build-out $75,000–$250,000; inventory $50,000–$200,000; staff $150,000+/year; legal/compliance $50,000+; plus $3,000 application + $15,000 licence fee. https://indicaonline.com/blog/how-to-open-a-dispensary-in-michigan/ — Accessed 2026-10-28.
Adult-use retailer — mid-range / high end $500,000–$750,000 mid; $1M+ high Same IndicaOnline page — Accessed 2026-10-28.
Adult-use retailer — alternative total range $200,000–$300,000 or more (narrower, licence + fit-out focused) IndicaOnline, "How to Get a Dispensary License in Michigan 2025" (same update window): https://indicaonline.com/blog/how-to-get-a-dispensary-license-in-michigan/ — Accessed 2026-10-28. The $200k–$300k and $300k–$1M+ ranges conflict because they use different scopes (fit-out only vs. first-year operating costs); do not average them.
Adult-use retailer — alternative total range $200,000–$750,000 IndicaOnline, "How Much Does It Cost to Open a Dispensary" (2026): https://indicaonline.com/blog/how-much-does-it-cost-to-open-a-dispensary-2026/ — Accessed 2026-10-28. Licensing fees in that summary ($6,000–$40,000) are a generic range, not the Michigan R. 420.7 schedule, and should not be quoted for Michigan.
Cultivation / processing / microbusiness startup [UNAVAILABLE] as a sourced Michigan-specific range No Michigan-specific, dated, non-official cultivation/processing startup range was found in this session that could be cited without inventing it. Do not extrapolate the retailer ranges to growers/processors.

Official costs that ARE part of startup (for budgeting, not estimates): $3,000 prequalification + the R. 420.7 licence fee (§4.1) or MMFLA assessment (§4.10) + municipal fee up to $5,000/year (MMFLA §205(2)) + $100,000 bodily-injury financial responsibility + (medical) $100,000 premises liability insurance + (medical) capitalisation in §4.12 + Metrc/POS, security, fire review, and inventory/testing costs. Social-equity reductions (§4.11) reduce only the CRA fees, not build-out, cameras, bond/insurance, or first inventory.

4.15 What is NOT a Michigan licence type (to prevent directory errors)

  • Delivery licence: does not exist (§4.5).
  • Wholesale licence: does not exist as a separate type; wholesaling is done under grower/processor/retailer/microbusiness licences. The 24% wholesale tax (2025 PA 23, eff. 1 Jan 2026) is a tax on wholesale transfers, not a licence type — full detail is Part 2.
  • Hemp retail/store licence: does not exist as a separate type; hemp retailing is covered by the CRA processor-handler licence (§4.13B).
  • Caregiver/patient registration: not a commercial licence (MMMA registry, Part 1/Part 5 counts only).
  • "Class D grower" or "nursery" licence: no such Michigan marihuana licence type in the CRA Municipal Guide or R. 420.7. If a directory lists one for Michigan, it is an error or an out-of-state type.

PART 5 — LICENCE DATA SOURCES

Reading guide. For each source: URL (verbatim from a search result or a document opened in this session — never guessed), holder type, format, access/download method, update frequency as stated by the source, latest data date actually seen in this session, fields available, and limitations. "Interactive search/dashboard, no download" is stated explicitly where that is the case. Where a direct download link and file name could be verified from a returned URL, it is given exactly; where only a hub page exists and the file name pattern must be inferred, that is marked [VERIFY] and no URL is invented. No individual licence holder is listed in this Part.

A note on "the CRA licensee list." Michigan does not publish, in this session's findings, a single downloadable CSV/XLSX master list of all active marihuana licensees by type and municipality. What exists is (1) monthly statistical PDFs with counts by type, (2) weekly licensing-report PDFs with recent approvals/renewals (a rolling window, not a master list), (3) a public verification search (MiCLEAR/Accela-based, record-by-record, no bulk download found), and (4) disciplinary/bulletin PDFs. A researcher who needs a near-complete roster must combine the weekly reports over time, scrape/verify record-by-record, or file a FOIA request — and must say so. Any third-party "Michigan licensee list" (e.g. CRB Monitor) is a commercial database, not an official source, and its totals conflict with CRA totals (see §5.8).

5.1 CRA statistical / monthly reports (the authoritative count source)

  • What it is: CRA Monthly Report, one PDF per month, with three sections: (1) Medical Marijuana Facility Licensing, (2) Adult-Use Establishment Licensing, (3) Medical Marijuana Registry Program. Each licensing section reports product sales, plants, packages/inventory, transfers, initial applications (received/approved/denied), renewal applications, active licences by type, application processing time, notices of non-compliance, complaints/investigations, disciplinary action, hearings, revenue/expenses, home-delivery approvals, sales by region, employees, and (adult-use) social-equity applications/education/assistance. The registry section reports registry applications, qualifying patients and primary caregivers approved in each county, cards revoked, conditions, certifying physicians, and registry revenue.
  • URL / hub: The CRA statistical-reports hub was cited in secondary sources with a legacy LARA URL (https://www.michigan.gov/lara/0,4601,7-154-89334_79571_93032-497635--,00.html) that is a pre-redesign URL and is not relied on here. Individual monthly PDFs live under the CRA media path. Direct download link verified by opening in this session — September 2025: File name: September-Monthly-Report-2025.pdf — URL: https://www.michigan.gov/cra/-/media/Project/Websites/cra/Agency-Reports/Statistical-Reports/monthly-report/September-Monthly-Report-2025.pdf — Accessed 2026-10-28 (crawled 2026-03-24 in the tool's copy; the PDF itself is dated September 1–30, 2025). Pattern for other months: A March 2025 file is cited in secondary literature as March-2025-Monthly-Report.pdf under .../Statistical-Reports/monthly-report/ — that filename pattern is not verified by a direct open in this session for months other than September 2025, so other months' exact URLs are [VERIFY] via the CRA statistical-reports hub on michigan.gov/cra rather than constructed here.
  • Format: PDF only (no CSV/XLSX download found for monthly reports). Tables are text-extractable but the "Active Licenses" tables are laid out as wrapped text in the PDF (see §5.2 for the parsed counts).
  • Access: Free, no login, direct PDF download via the URL above.
  • Update frequency as stated: Monthly (each report covers one calendar month; the September 2025 report is headed "September 1, 2025 – September 30, 2025").
  • Latest data date actually seen in this session: September 2025 (directly opened). Secondary sources report that CRA monthly files run through August 2026 (Divine Toke fall-2026 check-in: "Monthly files run through August 2026") and September 2026 (Divine Toke price page citing the CRA September 2026 monthly report: adult-use sales $242,263,191.56, adult-use flower $59.99/oz, medical $82.34/oz, medical sales $264,549.07). Those August/September 2026 files were not directly opened in this session, so their licence-count tables are reported in §5.2 only via the secondary (CannBus/Marijuana Herald) route and marked as such. The parent dossier should open the August and September 2026 PDFs directly before publishing 2026 counts as CRA-confirmed.
  • Fields available: See section list above. Licence counts are by type only — no licensee names, addresses or municipalities in the monthly report's count tables. (Licensee names appear only in the weekly licensing reports, §5.3, and in disciplinary orders, §5.5.)
  • Limitations: PDF-only; no bulk export; "active licences" is a point-in-time count at month-end and includes temporary-event licences then authorised (which expire with the event); social-equity licences are counted inside the type totals in the "Active Licenses" table and broken out only in the applications tables, so the monthly report does not give a clean "total social-equity licensees" stock figure.

The lesson is to always carry the month with the count.

5.3 CRA weekly licensing reports (recent approvals/renewals — the closest thing to a public licensee roster)

  • What it is: CRA Licensing Reports, published weekly, listing licensees whose licences were approved/renewed in that week, with entity name, licence number (e.g. AU-G-C-001355, AU-P-000458, AU-R-001104, AU-ER-002751), licence type, premises address (street, city, ZIP), and action/date (e.g. "CRA Approved Renewal," date).
  • Direct download link verified by search return in this session — October 2025 example: File name: Licensing-Report-10262025---11012025.pdf — URL: https://www.michigan.gov/cra/-/media/Project/Websites/cra/Agency-Reports/Licensing-Reports/AU-Licensing-Reports/2025/October/Licensing-Report-10262025---11012025.pdf — Accessed 2026-10-28 (returned by search; the PDF itself was not text-opened in this session beyond its search snippet, which shows the field layout above). The path pattern (AU-Licensing-Reports/2025/October/) suggests parallel medical reports exist, but no medical weekly-report URL was verified here — [VERIFY] via the CRA licensing-reports hub.
  • Format: PDF, weekly. No CSV/XLSX bulk download found.
  • Access: Free, no login, direct PDF download.
  • Update frequency as stated: Weekly (file name encodes the week, e.g. 26 Oct – 1 Nov 2025).
  • Latest data date actually seen: Week of 26 Oct – 1 Nov 2025 (the example above). No 2026 weekly report URL was verified in this session — [VERIFY] whether weekly reports continued into 2026 on the same path pattern; do not construct 2026 weekly URLs by analogy.
  • Fields available: Licensee/entity name, DBA/trade name where given, licence number, licence type, premises address, action (approved/renewal), action date. No ownership, no plant count, no sales data.
  • Limitations: Rolling window only — a single week's report is NOT a roster; reconstructing a roster requires collecting every weekly PDF and de-duplicating renewals vs. new approvals. A licence that was approved in an earlier week and not renewed in the current week will not appear. Do not present a weekly report as "the CRA licensee list."

5.4 CRA licensee verification search (Accela / MiCLEAR) — interactive search, NO bulk download

  • What it is: Michigan's licensing verification search, built on Accela (MiPLUS / Accela Citizen Access). LARA's own description: "Accela Citizen Access is a web portal that allows users to search for records, enforcement cases, and licensees" and "Licensing and registration records are made available on this website by LARA." For CRA licensees specifically, the CRA's disciplinary-report guidance directs users to "the MiCLEAR License Verification webpage, and input the licensee's name and profession or license number. Once the licensee's name appears, click on the name to bring up disciplinary information on this licensee if the Enforcement Action field contains a 'Yes.'" Source: LARA disciplinary page: https://www.michigan.gov/lara/bureau-list/cscl/complaints/disciplinary — Accessed 2026-10-28 (this page is the general LARA disciplinary page; the CRA-specific MiCLEAR verification flow is described on it).
  • URL: No CRA-specific MiCLEAR search URL was returned as a directly openable link in this session. The general entry points cited in LARA material are www.michigan.gov/miclear ("Verify a License") and the Accela host aca-prod.accela.com/MILARA (cited for MiPLUS account access). Both are given here as entry points to verify, not as verified CRA-search URLs — [VERIFY] the exact CRA verification search URL on michigan.gov/cra before publishing it. Do not publish aca-prod.accela.com/MILARA as "the CRA licensee search" without that check; it is the LARA MiPLUS/Accela host, and CRA marihuana licensing historically used its own Accela application portal (see below).
  • CRA application portal (distinct from verification search): Secondary CRA guidance states "Both stages of the application process will be completed online on your account on the Accela portal" (https://michigancannabis.org/business — Accessed 2026-10-28). The CRA Step 1 paper-application PDFs exist as a paper alternative, but the online route is Accela-based. No Accela export/download button for the full licensee roster was found or described in any source in this session; the portal is an application and record-by-record verification tool, not a bulk export. If the parent dossier needs to state an export option, it must be marked [UNAVAILABLE] pending a live portal check (which a text-fetch subagent cannot perform — see Research Notes).
  • Format: Interactive search (by name, licence number, profession/type). No CSV/XLSX/PDF roster download found.
  • Access: Public search; no login stated for verification. Account login required for applicants/licensees to manage their own records.
  • Update frequency: Continuous (record-by-record, as licences issue/renew/discipline).
  • Fields available (per record): Licensee name, licence type, licence number, issue/expiration dates, status, county (in MiPLUS records generally), enforcement/disciplinary flag and date of action where applicable.
  • Limitations: One record at a time; no "list all licensees in X municipality" bulk view found; disciplinary detail requires the separate DAR lookup by date (§5.5).

5.5 Disciplinary actions, fines, consent orders and final orders

  • CRA monthly disciplinary reporting (inside the monthly reports, §5.1): Each monthly report's licensing sections include "Disciplinary Action Taken by the CRA" tables (warning / formal complaint / consent order / final order, by licence type) and complaint/investigation counts. Example (directly opened): September 2025 adult-use disciplinary table shows Class C growers with 17 formal complaints + 5 consent orders; retailers 4 warnings + 17 formal complaints + 10 consent orders; processors 2 formal complaints + 5 consent orders — full table in the September 2025 PDF (URL §5.1). These are counts, not names.
  • CRA disciplinary action reports / orders (named licensees): Individual consent orders, stipulations and formal complaints are published as PDFs under the CRA Disciplinary-Actions media path. Example verified by search return: ENF-24-00816 (Michigan Pure Farms LLC) — URL pattern: https://sup1rpr1lh5l3porl3qi.vcsolaris.top/cra/-/media/Project/Websites/cra/Disciplinary-Actions/2025/April/Michigan-Pure-Farms-LLC-dba-Michigan-Pure-Pharms-AUGC001256-Consent-Order-and-Stipulation-and-Formal.pdf — Accessed 2026-10-28 (this is the state's CDN mirror host as returned by search; the michigan.gov/cra equivalent path was not separately verified — [VERIFY] the canonical michigan.gov URL before republishing). Fields: respondent name/DBA, licence numbers, premises address, violation counts with rule citations, sanction (fine, revocation, surrender, restriction).
  • Monthly disciplinary summaries in secondary reporting (for recent scale, not as official counts): July 2026: 75 enforcement actions dated in July 2026, including 3 surrenders (GCM Waypoint processor AU-P-000154, Bangor; Zaza Recreational retailer AU-R-001347, Flushing; Triforce Farm grower GR-A-000232, Pittsford), with Dragonfly Kitchen III Inc. (Cassopolis) accounting for 43 records. Source: https://www.mmjdaily.com/article/9866731/michigan-cra-issues-75-july-enforcement-actions-three-licenses-surrendered/ — Accessed 2026-10-28. October 2026 (secondary): GP Holdings LLC (Millie Montana Industries, Clare) — 20 medical Class C licences revoked (GR-C-000901 through GR-C-000924) + $2 million fine; Budbridge LLC retailer licence revoked 1 Oct 2026 + $251,250 fine; Michigan Investment 10 LLC adult-use + medical processor licences shut down eff. 24 Sept 2026 + $2 million fine. Sources: https://www.mmjdaily.com/article/9878333/michigan-cra-pulls-20-grower-licenses-from-gp-holdings-levies-2m-fine/ and https://news.crbmonitor.com/2026/10/from-mislabeled-mulch-to-cameras-facing-a-wall/ — both Accessed 2026-10-28. These October 2026 enforcement figures post-date the September 2025 CRA counts in §5.2 and partly explain the medical Class C decline; they are secondary-reported here and the underlying CRA final orders should be opened before the parent dossier quotes them as CRA-confirmed.
  • LARA Disciplinary Action Reports (DAR) hub: https://www.michigan.gov/lara/bureau-list/cscl/complaints/disciplinary — Accessed 2026-10-28. Format: fiscal-year/month PDFs (fiscal year 1 Oct – 30 Sept), searchable within the PDF by licensee name/number ("Edit, then Find"). To find an order you must first know its date of action from MiCLEAR (§5.4); open complaints do not appear. Limitation: this is the general LARA DAR system; CRA-specific monthly disciplinary summaries are the primary route for marihuana licensees, and the DAR hub's coverage of CRA orders vs. other LARA professions must be checked before citing it as a complete CRA disciplinary source.
  • Format summary: PDF (monthly counts + individual orders). No CSV/XLSX disciplinary export found. No download button beyond the PDF link itself.

5.6 Recalls, health advisories and bulletins

  • CRA Bulletins page: Secondary reporting states recall bulletins are published at "Michigan.gov/CRA/Bulletins" and searchable by Metrc tag number (Detroit Free Press via https://four20post.com/2024/05/michigans-cannabis-regulatory-agency-recalls-flavor-galaxys-infused-pre-rolled-joints/ — Accessed 2026-10-28). The bulletins page URL itself (michigan.gov/cra bulletins path) was not returned as a directly openable URL in this session — [VERIFY] the exact bulletins hub URL on michigan.gov/cra.
  • What bulletins contain: Product name, producer/processor and licence number, batch/package Metrc tag numbers, affected sales locations (retailers) and sale dates, reason (e.g. banned chemical residue above action limits, untested final-form product, excess THC, mislabelling), consumer instruction (return to retailer for disposal), and adverse-reaction reporting (CRA Adverse Reaction Reporting Form; CRA phone as published on bulletins).
  • Recent examples (secondary-reported, for scale only): Flavor Galaxy infused pre-rolls (Hazel Park processor; ~1,100 joints, 20 dispensaries; post-testing ingredient addition alleged); Flight Live Resin Disposable vapes (Sky Labs processor; Grease Monkey / Space Ether / Bubblegum; banned chemical residue); Fawn River Cultivation Hash Melts Green Crack 1G Live Rosin Dab (AU-P-000460; 786 units; CRA advisory 18 Sept 2026; banned chemical, substance not named). Sources: https://four20post.com/2024/05/michigans-cannabis-regulatory-agency-recalls-flavor-galaxys-infused-pre-rolled-joints/, https://cannabislaw.report/michigan-recalls-marijuana-vape-cartridges-for-possible-banned-chemical-residue/, https://themarijuanaherald.com/2026/09/michigan-recalls-786-marijuana-concentrates-after-testing-finds-banned-chemical/ — all Accessed 2026-10-28. Bulletin PDFs themselves were not opened here; do not quote batch/tag numbers from secondary summaries.
  • Format: PDF bulletins/advisories (individual, per recall). No consolidated recall CSV/XLSX found. No bulk download.
  • Limitation: There is no single "all Michigan cannabis recalls" dataset in this session's findings; completeness requires enumerating bulletins chronologically from the bulletins hub.

5.7 Patient and caregiver registry statistics (counts only — no individual data)

  • Source: CRA Monthly Report, Section 3 "Medical Marijuana Registry Program" (§5.1, same PDF). Fields: initial/renewal registry applications; qualifying patients and primary caregivers approved in each county (county table); registry cards revoked; nature of debilitating conditions; number of physicians providing written certifications; registry revenue/expenses; applications not processed within established time requirements.
  • Format: PDF (inside the monthly report). No separate registry CSV found.
  • Latest counts seen: September 2025 report's registry section was in the table of contents of the directly opened PDF, but its county table values were not extracted in this session (the PDF text window ended before the registry tables in the lines read). Therefore no September 2025 patient/caregiver count is published here from a direct open. Secondary-routed counts are: patients 59,337 (31 Dec 2025), 79,022 (31 Dec 2024), 116,856 (31 Dec 2023); caregivers 3,741 (31 Dec 2025), 9,647 (31 Dec 2023); certifying physicians 148 (31 Dec 2025); patients 50,975 and caregivers 2,916 (Aug 2026). Source: https://www.cannbus.org/cannmir/mi_cannmir.html — Accessed 2026-10-28. All of these are secondary-routed and [VERIFY] against the CRA monthly PDFs for those months. A conflicting secondary figure — a 2024 study summary claiming "nearly 110,000 active caregivers" vs. "roughly 35,000 authorized physicians" (https://cannabispromotions.com/news/article/study-medical-cannabis-caregivers-outnumber-clinicians-autho-2tw98048 — Accessed 2026-10-28) — is not compatible with CRA registry counts (caregivers ~3,741–9,647 in CRA-derived series) and appears to count a different population (possibly all persons ever registered, or a national/multi-state figure misattributed to Michigan). It is listed here only as a rejected figure; do not publish it as a Michigan caregiver count. The Senate Fiscal Agency historical series (patients 297,515 in 2018 falling to 195,776 in 2022; caregivers 43,056 in 2018 falling to 21,698 in 2022) is consistent in direction with the CRA-derived decline but uses fiscal-year definitions — source: https://sfa.senate.michigan.gov/Departments/DataCharts/DClar_MedicalMarihuanaParticipationData.pdf — Accessed 2026-10-28.
  • Limitation: Registry statistics are aggregate counts by county/condition; individual patient/caregiver identities are not public and must not be sought or published.

5.8 Municipality opt-out / authorisation lists

  • Official CRA list? [UNAVAILABLE as a single downloadable list in this session]. No CRA-published statewide "municipalities opted out of adult-use" CSV/PDF was returned as a directly openable URL in this session. The CRA Municipal Guide explains the mechanism (medical = opt-in ordinance; adult-use = may prohibit/limit by ordinance) and the attestation/notification process, but it does not itself list opted-out municipalities. The task instruction for Part 3 requires "the official CRA list … If it cannot be retrieved, say so and give the exact URL" — for Part 5, the finding is: no verified CRA opt-out list URL was retrieved in this session; the CRA statistical-reports hub on michigan.gov/cra and the CRA Municipal Guide are the places to re-check, and no URL is invented here. Secondary claims that "over 1,300 of 1,773 municipalities have opted out" (e.g. https://www.essencemichigan.com/cannabis-law-in-michigan/ — Accessed 2026-10-28) are un-sourced in that summary and are not adopted as an official count.
  • What does exist locally: Individual municipal ordinances and licence lists (see §5.11). The CRA's licensing process itself generates municipal authorisation evidence per application (Attestation I for medical; Municipality Notification / Notification of Noncompliance for adult-use), but those are per-application records, not a published statewide list.
  • Format if found: [UNAVAILABLE] — to be re-checked via live CRA site navigation (see Research Notes).

5.9 Hemp licence-holder data

  • MDARD grower / CRA processor-handler lists — NOT public in list form. MSU Extension's hemp FAQ, summarising MDARD's position, states: "Is there a list of growers, processors, or handlers available to the public in Michigan? No. Grower and processor-handler information is exempt from disclosure under PA 641 of 2018 and MDARD is prohibited from disclosing it." Source: https://msu-prod.dotcmscloud.com/hemp/index — Accessed 2026-10-28. (PA 641 of 2018 is the pre-2020 pilot act; the non-disclosure treatment under the current PA 220 / PA 547 regime is [VERIFY] against current MDARD guidance, but no public MDARD/CRA hemp roster was found in this session to contradict it.) Consequence for Part 5: there is no official downloadable Michigan hemp grower or processor-handler roster to inventory; the inventory entry is "no public list — exempt/non-disclosed," with the USDA route below as the only public record.
  • USDA hemp producer search (the public route for Michigan growers). USDA's Hemp Production Program publishes a public search tool for licensed producers nationwide; states/tribes report their licensees to USDA and USDA populates the tool, plus USDA-direct licensees where USDA runs the programme. Michigan growers appear as "licensed producers" (USDA term) / "registered hemp growers" (MDARD term). Tool URL as given in MDARD bulletins: hemp.ams.usda.gov/s/PublicSearchTool (cited at https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDARD/bulletins/338435f and https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDARD/bulletins/37870de — both Accessed 2026-10-28). Format: interactive search tool (search by name/business/state); no bulk CSV download described in those bulletins — marked as interactive search, no download found [VERIFY by opening the tool]. Fields (per USDA programme description): producer name/business, licence/registration number, status, location information as reported by the state. Limitation: the tool reflects what Michigan reports to USDA (monthly, per the Michigan State Hemp Plan: grower registration number, status and changes reported by the 1st of each month — https://www.ams.usda.gov/sites/default/files/media/MichiganStateHempPlan.pdf — Accessed 2026-10-28), so it may lag MDARD's internal register and it does not include CRA processor-handler licensees (who are not "producers" in USDA's sense).
  • USDA approved-plan list (not a licensee list, but the plan authority). https://www.ams.usda.gov/rules-regulations/hemp/state-and-tribal-plan-review — Accessed 2026-10-28; updated 17 Feb 2026; lists "Michigan — MI Approved Plan (pdf)." Format: HTML table + PDF plan documents. This confirms Michigan runs its own USDA-approved state plan (not the USDA direct-licensing programme) — cross-reference Part 7.

5.10 LARA Corporations Division / business entity search

  • What it is: Michigan Business Entity Search (MiBusiness Registry Portal), operated by LARA Corporations Division (now via the MiBusiness Registry Portal, live from 23 June 2025, replacing the older Corporations Division search). It covers business-entity registration (LLC/corporation status, registered agent, formation) — not marihuana licensure. A marihuana licensee's entity record here proves only that the entity exists and is in good standing as a business; it does not prove it holds a CRA licence, and a CRA licensee operating under a DBA may appear under a different legal name.
  • URL: Portal host cited in LARA material as mibusinessregistry.lara.state.mi.us ("Search for Michigan business information, including registration status and details, through the MiBusiness Registry Portal") — returned via search snippets, not directly opened here [VERIFY the exact search URL on michigan.gov/lara before publishing]. Format: interactive search (by entity name). No bulk download. Fields: entity name, entity type, status, formation date, registered agent/office (as applicable). Limitation: no licence-type, premises, or CRA-status fields; must be cross-checked against CRA verification (§5.4) before any entity is described as "licensed."

5.11 Local (city / village / township / county) licence and permit records — examples, not a statewide list

No statewide compilation of local cannabis licences exists in this session's findings. Local records are per-municipality, in different formats, and must be checked municipality by municipality (full local-rules analysis is Part 3). Examples verified in this session:

  • Detroit (Wayne County) — Office of Marijuana Ventures & Entrepreneurship (now Office of Cannabis Affairs, under Civil Rights, Inclusion & Opportunity). The city publishes award announcements as web pages (not a downloadable roster): first 33 adult-use retail licences under the revised ordinance (20 equity + 13 non-equity, with business names and street addresses) — https://detroitmi.gov/news/city-announces-recipients-first-33-adult-use-marijuana-retail-licenses-under-revised-ordinance — Accessed 2026-10-28. Format: HTML news page. Limitation: award announcements are snapshots; Detroit licences expire 30 September each year with renewals due 120 days prior (secondary summary, https://divinetoke.org/blog/detroit-social-equity-check-in-fall-2026/ — Accessed 2026-10-28 [VERIFY against Detroit's renewal page]), and no continuously updated Detroit licensee roster was found here. Detroit's second-round offering (30 retail + 10 microbusiness + 10 consumption-lounge licences, half equity) is described at https://beardbrospharms.com/detroit-opens-second-license-application-period/ — Accessed 2026-10-28 [secondary; verify against Detroit's own round-2 page].
  • Other municipalities: Local licence/permit records, where published, are typically found as (a) council meeting packets/minutes approving local licences, (b) municipal ordinance/code pages listing authorised licence caps, or (c) a city clerk's licence list. No other municipality's roster URL was verified in this session; Part 3's city-by-city check must enumerate them from municipal sites directly. Do not extrapolate Detroit's format to other municipalities.
  • County records: Counties do not issue marihuana licences; county relevance in Part 5 is limited to (a) Treasury excise-revenue distribution lists by municipality/county (Part 2, not a licence roster) and (b) registry statistics by county (§5.7).

5.12 Tribal licence records

  • Finding: [UNAVAILABLE] as a public inventory in this session. No Michigan tribal cannabis/hemp licence roster, tribal regulator licence-search portal, or tribal ordinance licence list was returned as a directly openable public source in this session. Tribal cannabis/hemp operations, compacts and ordinances are Part 10 of the full dossier and must be sourced from official tribal government sources and state-tribal agreements only. For Part 5, the inventory entry is: tribal licence records — no public source verified; do not substitute a commercial directory or a news list for a tribal record. If a tribe publishes a licence list, it will be a tribal-government source, not a CRA source, and must be cited as such.

5.13 Other CRA data products that touch licence data

  • CRA annual / fiscal-year reports (LARA boilerplate reports): e.g. FY2024 CRA Annual Report (Sec. 601/602) — https://www.michigan.gov/lara/-/media/Project/Websites/lara/about/Legislative-Reports/Boilerplate-Required-Reports/FY2024/Sec-601-and-602-CRA-Annual-Report.pdf — Accessed 2026-10-28. Format: PDF. Contains the fee table used in §4.10, application volumes, enforcement summaries, and demographic survey results (e.g. FY2024 survey sent to 2,484, 504 responses, 20.28% response rate). Limitation: annual, not a licence roster; demographic percentages from a low-response survey must not be presented as population shares without the response rate.
  • CRA bulletins / advisories (non-recall): e.g. wholesale-tax and hemp guidance bulletins on michigan.gov/cra and MDARD GovDelivery bulletins (hemp programme updates). Format: HTML/PDF bulletins. Not licence rosters, but they are the source for hemp fee/licence-year facts in §4.13.
  • Treasury adult-use marijuana distributions: Michigan Department of Treasury publishes fiscal-year distribution PDFs by municipality/county (e.g. FY2025 distributions, 24 Feb 2026, cited in MPP's tax-revenue survey: https://www.michigan.gov/treasury/-/media/Project/Websites/treasury/ORTA/Adult-Use-Marijuana/FY-2025/FY-2025-Adult-Use-Marijuana-Distributions-02-24-2026.pdf — Accessed 2026-10-28 via secondary citation [VERIFY by direct open]). Format: PDF. This is a revenue-share list (which municipalities/counties received excise distributions because they host licensed retailers), not a licence list — but it is the only official statewide list that indirectly evidences which municipalities host at least one licensed retailer. Limitation: it does not name licensees, licence types other than retail, or municipalities that authorise but have no operating retailer.

5.15 Method limits of this Part 5 inventory (read before reusing it)

  1. Text-fetch subagent limit: This research was done by web search + text fetch, not by live-browser navigation. Interactive tools (MiCLEAR/Accela search, USDA producer search tool, CRA statistical-reports hub navigation, CRA bulletins hub navigation) could not be operated or screenshot-verified. Every interactive source above is therefore inventoried from its description in official/secondary pages, not from a completed search inside the tool. The parent agent should run a live-browser check on: (a) the CRA statistical-reports hub to capture the August/September 2026 monthly PDFs and the current CRA opt-out list if one exists; (b) MiCLEAR to confirm the CRA verification search URL and whether any export exists; (c) the USDA producer tool filtered to Michigan; (d) the CRA bulletins hub.
  2. No FOIA data: No FOIA request was made. A FOIA request to the CRA for a machine-readable active-licensee extract (by type + municipality) is the recommended follow-up if the parent dossier needs a true roster.
  3. Counts are licence counts, not business counts: A single business holding stacked Class C licences, plus medical equivalents, plus a processor licence, appears multiple times in every CRA total. Never divide sales or revenue by "licence count" and call the result "per business" without stating the stacking caveat.

Rejected: the ~110,000 figure is incompatible with CRA registry counts and its population is undefined. - C9. Hemp grower fee: $100 (2019–2020 pilot) vs. $1,250 (current state-plan fee). Reconciled: $100 superseded. - C10. Startup totals: $200k–$300k vs. $300k–$1M+ for a retailer. Different scopes (fit-out vs. first-year operating) — present as a range of estimates with scopes, never as a single point estimate. - C11. Adult-use retailer "assessment $25,000" (older secondary sources) vs. $15,000 (current R. 420.7). Reconciled: $25,000 is pre-2022 tiered-system residue — rejected.

Part 6 — Market Data (Run 1)

Dossier date: 28 October 2026. Date accessed for every fact below: 2026-10-28, unless a source's own publication/update date is stated. Federal baseline (fixed context, not re-researched): state-licensed medical marijuana and FDA-approved products moved to Schedule III effective 28 April 2026 (91 FR 22714); adult-use remains Schedule I; 280E generally lifted for Schedule III medical activity, adult-use fully subject to 280E; hemp PL 119-37 §781 effective 12 November 2026, limited by PL 119-103 §2019 until 11 December 2026, after which the full total-THC definition and 0.4 mg total THC per container cap apply; USDA DEA-registered lab testing delayed to 31 December 2026; federal medical appropriations rider through 11 December 2026; no federal cannabis banking law. No contradiction to that baseline was found in the market sources used here. Market figures below are sales/price/licence data, not tax-law conclusions; the 24% wholesale tax (effective 1 January 2026, under litigation — see Part 2) is mentioned only where a market source ties it to sales or prices.

Method and access limitation — read first

  • The primary source for almost every figure in §§6.1–6.5 is the Michigan Cannabis Regulatory Agency (CRA) Monthly Statistical Report series, published at michigan.gov/cra (CRA statistical reports index). Direct opening of the CRA statistical-report index page was attempted in this session and returned HTTP 403 (access denied); it was not retried. The CRA December 2025 monthly report PDF link that appears in secondary discussion — https://www.michigan.gov/cra/-/media/Project/Websites/cra/Agency-Reports/Statistical-Reports/monthly-report/December-2025-Monthly-Report.pdf — was likewise not directly opened in this session. Figures attributed to "CRA monthly report" below therefore rest on (a) the MichiganCannabis.org sales and patient tables, which state their source as the CRA and were directly opened and read, and (b) reputable secondary republication of CRA reports (The Marijuana Herald, MJBizDaily, Cannabis Business Times, MLive via Ganjapreneur/WBET, New Cannabis Ventures), each dated below. Where a figure comes only via a secondary republication, that is stated. Do not treat a secondary republication as a substitute for the CRA PDF in the compiled dossier without a direct CRA check by the parent.
  • All dollar figures are retail sales as reported by CRA, not tax collections, unless stated.
  • "Adult-use" = MRTMA (2018) market; "medical" in CRA monthly sales tables = MMFLA facility sales (provisioning centres etc.), NOT caregiver transfers or unlicensed sales. That distinction explains why medical facility sales are now a fraction of a percent of the total while registered patients still number ~51,000: most registered patients evidently buy in the adult-use channel (see §6.6).
  • County names are given where a source gives them; statewide figures have no county.

6.5 Market saturation — what official/industry sources actually say

Do not invent saturation analysis. The sourced claims are: - Oversupply / unlimited licences: Cannabis Business Times, March 2026, reporting CRA: "low prices caused by oversupply in Michigan's unlimited license market"; the February 2026 sales dip was "a result of lower prices, not lower demand" (flower pounds +3.2% YoY while revenue fell) — https://www.cannabisbusinesstimes.com/us-states/michigan/news/15819825/michigan-cannabis-prices-remain-down-demand-steady-in-2026-despite-new-tax - Inventory overhang (2024): CRA via Cannabis Business Times, May 2024: adult-use flower inventory April 2024 696,472 lb total (growers 189,290 lb; retailers 143,332 lb; processors 176,273 lb; fresh-frozen at processors 187,578 lb), +40.5% vs April 2023 (495,863 lb) — https://Www.cannabisbusinesstimes.com/us-states/michigan/news/15686678/michigans-adult-use-cannabis-sales-up-21-from-last-year . No 2025/2026 inventory total was found in sources opened — [UNAVAILABLE] for a current inventory figure. - "Market maturation": CRA spokesman David Harns to MLive (via Ganjapreneur, Jan 2026): "a period of market maturation after several years of rapid growth"; "It was clear that this industry was not going to expand in perpetuity." - Consolidation/closures: MJBizDaily, Jan 2026: "price compression led to retail closures" (848 → 838 stores); "some asking for license caps to help stabilize prices"; Metro Times/Crain's: >940 licences inactive since 2019, closures increasing as margins shrink and supply outpaces demand. - Wholesale-tax overlay (2026, for Part 2 cross-reference, not a saturation finding on its own): 24% wholesale tax effective 1 January 2026; Treasury collections $37.38m in Q2 2026 and $73.4m through Q2 vs ~$105m/quarter projection (CannBus, citing Treasury/press; MJBizDaily May 2026: ~$34m through 30 April vs ~$105m quarterly target; House Fiscal Agency ~$420m/year estimate). Cannabis Business Times, March 2026: fear the tax would spike retail prices / crater demand "has yet to ring true through the first two months of 2026" — prices kept falling on oversupply. A repeal bill (HB 6224, Rep. James DeSana, introduced August 2026, per CannBus) and a second MiCIA Court of Claims suit (27 March 2026, "tax on a tax") are pending — full status is Part 2's job, not Part 6's. - National position: Michigan is the second-largest adult-use market in the US behind California (MJBizDaily Jan 2026; Grand View Research cannabis-tourism report, accessed 2026-10-28, repeats the $3.17bn 2025 figure and second-only-to-California ranking — https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/cannabis-tourism-market-report — secondary, commercial research firm, use only for the ranking claim, not for Michigan law). - No official CRA "saturation index," per-capita sales, or county concentration ranking was found in sources opened. Business concentration by municipality is Part 3's job; a secondary directory claim (Sativa University, undated, listing Detroit 72, Battle Creek 29, Grand Rapids 28, New Buffalo 28, Ann Arbor 26, Lansing 26 dispensaries — https://sativauniversity.com/cannabis-laws/michigan/ ) is NOT used as a concentration finding here because it is an undated secondary directory count, not an official source — flagged for Part 3 to verify or drop.

6.6 Decline of the medical market and caregiver numbers

Medical facility sales collapse

Medical facility sales fell from $481,225,496 in 2021 (26.8% of combined sales that year) to $256,017,177 in 2022, $80,756,000 in 2023, $17,960,037 in 2024, and $6,113,681 in 2025 (0.19% of combined 2025 sales). In 2026, January–September medical facility sales total $3,087,194 (calculated from monthly table), i.e. 0.14% of combined Jan–Sep 2026 sales. Monthly medical sales fell from $2,523,334 in January 2024 to $264,549 in September 2026. Sources: MichiganCannabis.org table + Herald monthly reports, all above. MJBizDaily, February 2025 (secondary): Michigan medical patient count fell to 79,022 in December 2024, down 71% since adult-use sales launched in December 2019; medical sales "now accounting for less than 1% of total cannabis sales"; many former patients now buy as adult-use consumers ("It's not like the medical patients are shrinking, the registries are shrinking" — Narmin Jarrous, Exclusive Brands) — https://mjbizdaily.com/news/medical-cannabis-registries-show-steep-decline-after-adult-use-sales-begin/401676/

Registered patients (CRA via MichiganCannabis.org patient table, opened 2026-10-28, last updated 6 October 2026, source stated as CRA)

Monthly registered patients, January 2020–August 2026 (December values bold in the source table; full monthly series opened): - Dec 2020: 243,372; Dec 2021: 237,741; Dec 2022: 179,863; Dec 2023: 116,856; Dec 2024: 79,022; Dec 2025: 59,337; Aug 2026 (latest): 50,975. - 2026 monthly: Jan 58,514; Feb 57,313; Mar 55,848; Apr 54,698; May 53,645; Jun 52,984; Jul 52,115; Aug 50,975. - 2025 monthly: Jan 76,693 → Dec 59,337 (a fall of 17,356 in the year; the December 2025 CRA report discussion on Overgrow, January 2026, citing the CRA December 2025 PDF, gives the same Dec 2025 figure and a −19,685 / −25% year change vs Dec 2024 — https://overgrow.com/t/michigan-community/19634?page=23 — secondary forum discussion of the CRA PDF, used only as corroboration). - CannBus calculation: patients fell 56% from Dec 2023 (116,856) to Aug 2026 (50,975). - County extremes (from the same patient table, latest year shown): Wayne County (Wayne County, MI) highest — 47,782 in 2019 → 9,243 in the latest column (2026); Oakland County next — 36,917 in 2019 → 7,188 in 2026; Ontonagon County and Keweenaw County lowest, never exceeding 200 in the years shown (Ontonagon 17 in 2026 column; Keweenaw 67). Caution: the county table's columns are labelled by year but the underlying CRA county snapshot date is not stated in the opened page; the Macomb County row shows an anomalous 1,485 for 2024 against 12,068 in 2023 and 6,200 in 2025, which looks like a data-entry or snapshot artefact — [VERIFY] before republishing any county figure, and do not use the county table for a trend claim. Source: https://michigancannabis.org/medical/statistics

Registered primary caregivers

  • Dec 2023: 9,647 (CannBus, citing CRA Dec 2023 report).
  • Dec 2024: 5,646 (Overgrow discussion of CRA December 2024/2025 reports, January 2026 — secondary; the CRA December 2025 discussion states Dec 2025 caregivers 3,741 and a −1,905 / −34% change vs 2024, which arithmetically implies 5,646 for Dec 2024 — consistent).
  • Dec 2025: 3,741 (CannBus, citing CRA Dec 2025 report; corroborated by the Overgrow CRA-PDF discussion).
  • Aug 2026: 2,916 (CannBus, citing CRA Aug 2026 report via Herald).
  • Certifying physicians, Dec 2025: 148 (CannBus, citing CRA Dec 2025 report; same figure in Overgrow discussion). Most common qualifying condition, Dec 2024: chronic pain, 63.10% of registrations (CannBus, citing CRA).
  • Historical context (Senate Fiscal Agency medical marihuana participation chart, via sfa.senate.michigan.gov PDF, search extract): patients peaked at 297,515 in FY2018 with 43,056 caregivers; by FY2022 patients 195,776, caregivers 21,698 — https://sfa.senate.michigan.gov/Departments/DataCharts/DClar_MedicalMarihuanaParticipationData.pdf . The FY series and the calendar-month CRA series are different bases; do not splice them.
  • A September 2026 secondary article claiming "nearly 110,000 active caregivers vs ~35,000 clinicians" nationally (Cannabis Promotions, citing an Annals of Internal Medicine study of 2024 public records) is NOT a Michigan caregiver count and must not be used for Michigan — it is flagged here only to prevent misattribution. Michigan caregivers at Aug 2026 are 2,916 per CRA via CannBus, two orders of magnitude below that national figure.
  • Provisioning centres: 100 at Dec 2025 (CannBus, CRA Dec 2025 report) vs 296 medical-licensed stores claimed in an undated secondary news page (MiMJNews — https://mimjnews.com/category/business-industry?page=31 ) vs 704 recreational stores in the same page — conflict, unresolved: the CRA-derived 100 provisioning-centre licences (Dec 2025) is preferred over the undated secondary "296 stores" claim, which may count dual-licensed storefronts or an earlier date. [VERIFY] against the CRA licence list (Part 5).
  • Why the registry shrinks while adult-use grows: the sources above point to patients migrating to the adult-use channel (no registry, no certification cost, lower prices, wider store network) rather than to falling cannabis use — but that is industry interpretation (Jarrous/MJBizDaily), not a CRA finding. State it as such.

  • Programme-end rationale (MDARD, via Morning Ag Clips/MJBizDaily/Hemp Today, Nov–Dec 2024): programme "no longer financially sustainable" as grower numbers fell 631 (2020) → 34 (2024); plus time/expense of investigating farms allegedly growing marijuana under the guise of hemp. Legislation cited: HB 5977 (introduced October 2024) to rescind Public Act 220 and dissolve the industrial hemp fund; MDARD said at the time "this is only a proposed change" and it would work with USDA on transition. Highly Capitalized (secondary, 2024/2025) states the transfer took effect 1 January 2025 and HB 5977 (2024) did not become law and did not dissolve the fund — https://highlycapitalized.com/michigan-transfers-hemp-regulation-to-usda/ . USDA-programme differences cited by MDARD: no licence fee, licences valid 3 years, growers must contract with USDA-certified sampling agents and DEA-registered labs for THC testing (with the federal DEA-lab enforcement delay to 31 December 2026 from the fixed baseline).

Bill numbers, text and status must be confirmed on legislature.mi.gov in Part 1 — not confirmed here.

That absence is itself a finding: do not import a national CBD market figure as a Michigan figure.
  • National context only (do not attribute to Michigan): USDA NASS estimated total US hemp production value at $238m in 2022 (NASS Great Lakes release, Jan 2024, above). US planted area for all utilizations in 2022: 28,314 acres; harvested 18,251 acres.
  • Secondary Michigan hemp-market claims found: none with a Michigan-specific dollar figure and a stated methodology survived the sourcing rule, so none is reported. Any Michigan hemp/CBD dollar figure in the compiled dossier must be newly sourced and marked secondary, or omitted with this [UNAVAILABLE] note.
  • Intoxicating hemp-derived cannabinoids sold through CRA licensees are, after the relevant CRA rules, marijuana-market sales for reporting purposes — see Part 1. No separate intoxicating-hemp sales split was found in CRA monthly reports opened via republication — [UNAVAILABLE].
